betaLB

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan 2026-11-23 03:19:07

Description

Generates profile likelihood confidence intervals for standardized regression coefficients (beta) and other effect sizes, including multiple correlation, semipartial correlations, improvement in R-squared, squared partial correlations, differences in standardized regression coefficients, and Cohen’s f-squared, for models fitted by lm(). The intervals invert the Gaussian likelihood-ratio test of the covariance matrix of the outcome and the regressors, with a normal-theory or a robust (fourth-moment) cutoff.

Installation

You can install the development version of betaLB from GitHub with:

if (!require("pak")) install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("jeksterslab/betaLB")

Example

In this example, a multiple regression model is fitted using program quality ratings (QUALITY) as the regressand/outcome variable and number of published articles attributed to the program faculty members (NARTIC), percent of faculty members holding research grants (PCTGRT), and percentage of program graduates who received support (PCTSUPP) as regressor/predictor variables using a data set from 1982 ratings of 46 doctoral programs in psychology in the USA (National Research Council, 1982). Likelihood-based confidence intervals for the standardized regression coefficients are generated using the BetaLB() function from the betaLB package.

library(package = betaLB)
df <- betaLB::nas1982

Fit the regression model using the lm() function. 

object <- stats::lm(formula = QUALITY ~ NARTIC + PCTGRT + PCTSUPP, data = df)

Estimate the standardized regression slopes and the corresponding likelihood-based confidence intervals. 

BetaLB(object = object, type = "mvn", alpha = 0.05)
#> Call:
#> BetaLB(object = object, type = "mvn", alpha = 0.05)
#> 
#> Standardized regression slopes with MVN likelihood intervals:
#>            est   2.5%  97.5%
#> NARTIC  0.4951 0.3423 0.6394
#> PCTGRT  0.3915 0.2395 0.5426
#> PCTSUPP 0.2632 0.1179 0.4148

Other Features

The package provides the following functions.

Function Purpose
BetaLB() Standardized regression coefficients with normal-theory (type = "mvn") or robust (type = "robust") likelihood intervals
RSqLB() R-squared and adjusted R-squared
DiffBetaLB() Differences of standardized regression coefficients
SCorLB() Semipartial correlations
SCorSqLB() Squared semipartial correlations (squared signed interval)
PCorLB() Squared partial correlations
DeltaRSqLB() Improvement in R-squared
FSqLB() Cohen’s f-squared and local f-squared

The coef(), confint(), summary(), and print() methods are available for the returned objects. The effect-size functions take the output of BetaLB() and use its type and control. Scalar targets use profile-likelihood regions; multi-coefficient targets use a conservative vector projection, and the output names the calibration and its dimension. An unverified endpoint is NA; no Wald endpoint is substituted. Robust calibration assumes independently sampled random regressors and finite fourth moments. Examples for each function are in the package vignettes.

Effect Sizes

The definitions, formulas, and notes on the intervals are in the help pages of the functions and in the vignette betaLB: Example Using the Effect Size Functions.
